items.title: Madras HC quashes 2023 FIR against 304 Hindu Munnani Deepathoon protesters
items.summary: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Thursday, September 24, quashed an FIR registered against more than 300 Hindu Munnani functionaries who protested in Madurai over the non-lighting of the Karthigai Deepam on the Thiruparankundram hill. The court was hearing a petition filed by S Nallathambi, one of the accused, seeking to quash the case registered by the Madurai city police. The FIR named the petitioner and 303 others as having allegedly assembled unlawfully and raised slogans against the State government around 5 pm on November 25, 2023. The protesters were opposing the decision not to light the Karthigai Deepam on Thiruparankundram hill. Police subsequently arrested them and registered a case against them. The petitioner's counsel argued that the protest was a form of democratic expression and that there had been no inconvenience to the general public or damage to public property. items.title: Karnataka forms SIT to reinvestigate Sowjanya rape and murder case
items.summary: The Karnataka government has constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to conduct a fresh investigation into the 2012 rape and murder case of 17-year-old Sowjanya in Dakshina Kannada’s Belthangady, following a direction from the Supreme Court. The SIT was formed through a government order dated September 24, a day after the Supreme Court’s direction. The Supreme Court had ordered a de novo investigation into the brutal rape and murder, originally registered by Belthangady police and later re-registered by the CBI’s Special Crime Branch in Chennai. The five-member SIT will be headed by Inspector General of Police(IGP) N Shashi Kumar, with CH Sudheer Kumar Reddy, DIG and police commissioner of Mangaluru City, Nisha James, SP, Intelligence Bengaluru, Lokesh Jagalasar, SP, CID Bengaluru and Venkatesh Prasanna, Additional SP Bengaluru Rural as members. The Supreme Court had specifically directed that officers who were part of the earlier investigations by Belthangady Police, the CID or the CBI should not be included in the new SIT. items.title: Kerala HC finds most POCSO courts lack mandated facilities, seeks affidavit on additional courts
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has found that most of the courts handling cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act in the state do not conform to statutory guidelines and lack adequate facilities. A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar V M issued the direction while considering a public interest litigation filed by the District Court Bar Association. The court directed the respondent Registrar (District Judiciary) to file an affidavit detailing the number of additional courts required to deal with POCSO cases, taking into account a Supreme Court judgment on the issue and the practices followed by different High Courts. The Bench said its own visits to district courts had revealed shortcomings in the functioning of POCSO courts. “During the visit to the District Courts, we found that most of the POCSO courts do not conform to the guidelines specified under the POCSO Act. The facilities are also inadequate.” The affidavit must also identify the courts currently trying POCSO cases that do not comply with the guidelines. items.title: Calcutta High Court grants relief to ABP editor, journalist in FIR over ‘Gerua Gundami’ headline
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Thursday granted interim relief to the editor and a journalist of Anandabazar Patrika (ABP) from coercive action in a First Information Report (FIR) registered against them over the newspaper's use of the expression “Gerua Gundami” (Saffron Hooliganism) in a news headline [Ishani Datta Ray & Anr. v The State of West Bengal & Ors.] . The newspaper had used the expression to describe violence that unfolded at the Jadavpur University on August 20. Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya granted interim relief to the accused after noting that the journalists had appeared before the police in response to notices issued during the investigation and had complied with them. During the hearing, the State also submitted that custodial interrogation of the journalists was not required. Taking note of the submissions, the Court directed the police not to take coercive action. "Concerned police authorities are directed not to take coercive steps against petitioners till 15th December, 2026 or until further order, whichever is earlier. items.title: After 5 infants die in fire, Telangana govt releases Rs 11.1 crore for RIMS renovation
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Three days after a fire accident claimed the lives of five infants, the Telangana government on Thursday, September 24, released Rs 11.1 crore for urgent repairs and renovation work at Adilabad’s Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS). Of the sanctioned funds, Rs 1 crore will be used to renovate the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU), while another Rs 1 crore has been set aside for repainting the hospital. Rs 1.6 crore will go towards repairs to the CC pavement and the damaged compound wall on the RIMS campus. A separate Rs 5 crore allocation has been made for repairs and upkeep of toilets and bathrooms. The government has also approved Rs 1.5 crore for immediate repairs to the oxygen pipeline network and Rs 1 crore for electrical works. Telangana health minister Damodara Raja Narasimha also instructed officials to complete fire, electrical and structural safety audits of all government hospitals within a month, with inspections being carried out every six months.
